digest.component_or_area: close event STATUS metadata and state reduction
propositions: A close without a completion signature appended is indistinguishable from a close executed with the gate disabled because both collapse to a single state in the current reader

The gate state (ENABLED/DISABLED/UNREADABLE) is read and discarded during close, so a later reader cannot discriminate between gate-off, force-close, local unattested close, signature-append failure, and config-unreadable fail-open closes

The completion_expectation enum (8 values: required, disposition, gate_off, gate_unreadable, force_bypassed, local_source, not_certifiable, not_applicable) must be persisted as a present-only field on the *->closed STATUS event in the same locked write as the close to durably record why a completion signature was or was not expected

A later reader combining the durable completion_expectation with the durable attestation can now distinguish required+attestation (signed), required+none (signature lost), disposition±attestation (disposition-signed or lost), and any other value (not expected, with the reason explicit in the enum value)

The completion_expectation derivation must visit gate state first (matching _completion_precheck branch order) so a forced close under disabled or unreadable config records gate_off or gate_unreadable respectively, never force_bypassed masking a fault

The idea->closed transition records not_applicable explicitly in close_ticket (the sole owner of that path) and never enters _completion_precheck, ensuring REJECT/DROP closes are never conflated with completion closes
